audit.summary: Archived assessment: Major. Theorem4.2 pure-direction improvement is false; Theorem4.6 optimistic advantage is discontinuous in a simplified game.
limitations: P1 — Theorem4.2 pure-direction improvement is false — Counterreading: Diversity/random population expansion may escape; no claim full stochastic method never converges.

P1 — Theorem4.2 pure-direction improvement is false — Counterevidence and scope: Concavity permits an improving mixture without improving any vertex direction at a nonsmooth point. AppendixA.5 positive-inner-product step does not imply Eq19. Random/diversity/population expansion branches in Algorithm2 can escape, so no full-algorithm nonconvergence claim follows.
P2 — Theorem4.6 optimistic advantage is discontinuous in a simplified game — Counterreading: Strict-best-response regions are locally linear; that does not imply global Lipschitzness.

P2 — Theorem4.6 optimistic advantage is discontinuous in a simplified game — Counterevidence and scope: Local affine behavior in a strict-response region is true but not global Lipschitzness. The zero-sum min-of-linear proof depends on equality of own rewards across best responses, absent here. Simplification and an interior switch do not prevent the jump.
